title: How to Brief a Freelancer to Name Your Business or Product
h1: How to brief a freelancer to name your business or product
description: Prepare a naming project: what the name must convey, audience, tone, length, languages, domain needs, names to avoid and how to check availability.
intro: A name is one of the few brand decisions that is hard to change later. Naming freelancers can generate creative, memorable options, but without a clear brief they produce long lists that miss the point. Good naming projects begin with a clear picture of what the name must do, who will hear it and practical limits such as domain names and languages. This article explains what to prepare and how to evaluate the names you receive.

faq.q: How many name options should I expect?
faq.a: Often a shortlist of 5 to 30, depending on the package. Quality matters more than quantity.
Usually only basic checks. For legal clearance, consult a trademark professional.

faq.q: Do I need the exact domain name?
faq.a: Not always. Many brands use a short addition, but the core name should be easy to find.

faq.q: Should the name describe what we do?
faq.a: Descriptive names are clear but harder to protect; invented names are distinctive but need more explanation.

faq.q: How do I choose between finalists?
faq.a: Say them aloud, test them with real customers and check availability before deciding.
